title: Avoiding the Reverse Fall Mistake in Drainage
description: One of the most frequent installation errors in drainage systems is failing to maintain a consistent downward slope, resulting in what professionals call reverse fall or counter-slope. When a drainage pipe dips or runs level instead of sloping downward toward the main line, wastewater fails to drain completely. This stagnation leads to a buildup of solid waste, chronic clogs, and foul odors escaping into the building. Proper installation requires checking alignment with a spirit level and securing hangers at correct intervals to prevent pipe sagging over time. Learning to identify and prevent reverse fall ensures long-term system reliability and protects your installation reputation.

Avoiding the Reverse Fall Mistake in Drainage

One of the most frequent installation errors in drainage systems is failing to maintain a consistent downward slope, resulting in what professionals call reverse fall or counter-slope. When a drainage pipe dips or runs level instead of sloping downward toward the main line, wastewater fails to drain completely. This stagnation leads to a buildup of solid waste, chronic clogs, and foul odors escaping into the building. Proper installation requires checking alignment with a spirit level and securing hangers at correct intervals to prevent pipe sagging over time. Learning to identify and prevent reverse fall ensures long-term system reliability and protects your installation reputation.
